text:
evan: heads-up — replay harness numbers are ~20% slower than synthetic for the same qps and payloads. digging in now, but posting findings here.

mira: hmm. are you running the same keepalive/conn pooling settings between runs?

evan: yes. harness config: keepalive=60s, max_conns=50, pipelined=false. replay uses real client timings (short think times) vs synthetic constant.

sam: can you paste the actual p95/p99?

evan: synthetic: p95=72ms, p99=120ms. replay: p95=92ms, p99=170ms. throughput identical.

jen: those tails smell like connection churn / TLS handshakes or contention. did you trace socket reuse?

evan: running ss -nt on server while replaying — seeing bursts of many TIME_WAIT and new sockets per second when replay uses many short lived sessions.

mira: that's the classic short-lived client pattern. also check TLS session resumption: if clients don't resume, handshake cost adds 30-60ms depending on CPU.

perf-bot: profile uploaded: s3://perf-artifacts/1937654321/flame.html

evan: flame shows a lot of kernel time in crypto_openssl and epoll_wait. off-CPU stacks show queuing in accept4 and recvmsg.

sam: did you compare gRPC vs REST? gRPC with long-lived channels should amortize TLS/Nagle etc.

evan: we tried both. with long-lived gRPC channels p95 matches synthetic. with short-lived HTTP/1.1 connections p99 regresses.

mira: also check TCP_NODELAY and Nagle—small requests + Nagle can add batching delays if delayed-acks interact badly.

jen: small experiment: disable Nagle (TCP_NODELAY=1) on client harness and enable keepalive to 300s, see if tails drop.

evan: did that — p95 improved by ~8ms, p99 improved by ~12ms, but still not fully aligned.

sam: could KV cache behavior be different? replay might miss prefix hits causing longer decode times and different kernel paths.

evan: confirmed: heatmap shows lower KV cache hit rate during replay (real sessions have different prompting distribution). cold KV lookups trigger extra memcpy and memory-bandwidth pressure.

mira: for apples-to-apples we need: identical batch size distribution, same sequence length distribution, same connection lifetime, and same keepalive. otherwise kernel selection and batching heuristics behave differently.

jen: on kernel selection: the runtime auto-selects AVX512 kernels when sequence length > 1024 or certain perf patterns detected. any chance replay triggers a different code path?

evan: yep. perf counters show the runtime picked a larger-kernel path mid-run leading to a temporary throughput dip as JIT/conv kernels warmed.

sam: is there an env to pin the kernel selection? might be useful for debugging.

evan: set REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=basic to force conservative kernels. after pinning, replay p95 fell back to 80ms (closer).

perf-bot: note: kernel-change events logged at 1937654356, 1937654368

mira: that explains spikes. we should avoid autoswitching during steady-state bench or record marker events.

jen: another angle — gRPC connection pooling and HPACK/flow-control can interact with batching heuristics. if many small streams are opened, the runtime's continuous-batching struggles to form good batches which pushes more work to single-token kernel paths.

evan: true. I saw average batch size drop from 6->2 under replay short sessions.

sam: recommendation checklist for reproducible apples-to-apples: 1) identical connection lifetime and keepalive 2) identical TLS resumption settings 3) same client-side pooling/threads 4) same prompt distribution & padding 5) pin kernel selection or warm-run until no kernel events 6) capture KV cache warmup profile

mira: add to that: measure socket churn (TIME_WAIT/sec) and TLS full-handshake rate. both are easy to miss.

jen: small useful commands to capture: 
```
ss -tan | grep ESTAB | wc -l   # active conns
ss -tan state time-wait | wc -l # TIME_WAIT
openssl s_time -connect host:443 -new  # TLS connect timing (sample)
```

evan: also ran ghz for gRPC long-lived channels: `ghz --concurrency 50 --connections 10` vs `--connections 50` changed behavior a lot. we should document default harness flags.

perf-bot: experiment saved as /bench/experiments/1937654321/meta.json

mira: action: evan to produce a minimal repro harness that toggles: keepalive, TCP_NODELAY, connection count, kernel pin, and KV warm state. put instructions in the bench repo.

evan: will do. quick note — disabling kernel auto-switch removed the mid-run dip but overall latency slightly higher; autoswitch improves steady-state but confounds apples-to-apples unless warmed.

sam: final thought: when reporting perf to product, always include: client lifecycle, TLS/resume rate, avg batch size, KV hit%, kernel-switch events. otherwise numbers are noise. :+1:

jen: thanks everyone. evan please drop the repro PR with steps and a short writeup.
evan: PR incoming, will link when ready.
